issues.detail: The Hebrew text says 'בֶּצֶר' (Bezer), but the Chinese renders it as '比色' (Bǐsè). The standard Chinese transliteration for Bezer is '比悉' or '比色' — however, the issue is that the Chinese adds '以巴衛' (Yǐbāwèi) at the beginning, which has no basis in the Hebrew text. The Hebrew begins with 'וּמֵעֵבֶר' (and from beyond/on the other side of), with no mention of '以巴衛' (which appears to be a transliteration of 'Eber' or a similar name not present here). This is an addition of a proper name not in the source.
